fields.Participants: CMO, Category Managers, VP Merchandising, Vendor Marketing
fields.Trigger: Annual vendor negotiation; new vendor onboarding

workflows.name: Co-Op Advertising Fund Agreement & Budget Allocation

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "print catalogs, social media ads, in-store displays, events, TV/radio, digital…" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documentation requirements" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-log of "CMO allocates co-op budget across marketing calendar" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-359 (ensure controlled execution — Co-Op Marketing & Promotional Fund Management (PA-39.2).)
- operational: CMO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Use-it-or-lose-it risk**: fund balances expire unspent for lack of planned activity; mitigated by calendar-based allocation at agreement setup (step 3)
- **Non-qualifying spend risk**: activities charged to the fund that the agreement disallows; mitigated by approved-activity-type setup with pre-approval rules (step 2)
System Touchpoints: - Co-op fund agreement setup — fund as % of purchases, approved activity types, pre-approval rules (steps 1–2)
- Co-op budget allocation across the marketing calendar (step 3)
Time Estimate: Per co-op agreement: negotiation within merchandising cycles + system setup 30 min ≈ 0.5–1 day of effort × ~50–80 agreements/year ≈ 25–80 days/year; quarterly co-op budget allocation across the marketing calendar.

steps.activity: CMO and VP Merchandising negotiate co-op advertising fund agreements with key vendors: (a) fund structure: % of purchases (typically 1–3%) or fixed annual budget, (b) eligible activities: print catalogs, social media ads, in-store displays, events, TV/radio, digital banners, (c) approval process: BuildRight proposes activity → vendor approves → execute → submit proof → vendor reimburses, (d) pre-approval: some vendors require pre-approval of all activities; others allow post-execution claim, (e) fund cap: maximum annual co-op spend per vendor, (f) carry-over: unused funds expire or roll to next year (vendor-specific)

System setup: co-op marketing fund per vendor: (a) annual budget/fund amount, (b) approved activity types, (c) pre-approval requirement flag, (d) reimbursement rate (% of cost covered, typically 50–100%), (e) documentation requirements

CMO allocates co-op budget across marketing calendar: (a) bi-monthly catalog: vendor co-op for product feature space (full page: PHP 50–100K; half page: PHP 25–50K), (b) social media campaigns: vendor co-op for sponsored posts, (c) in-store displays: vendor co-op for endcap and feature display materials, (d) events: vendor co-op for workshop sponsorship per W12.3, (e) seasonal campaigns: vendor co-op for holiday promotions

fields.Participants: CMO, Category Managers, VP Merchandising, key vendors

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "For each promotional event" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System workflow notification of "contact vendors with promotional proposals" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-compile of "compiles vendor commitments into promotional plan" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-359 (ensure controlled execution — Co-Op Marketing & Promotional Fund Management (PA-39.2).)
- operational: standard operating procedures; system-enforced validation rules
Pain Points / Risks: - **Overpromised-funding risk**: plans built on verbal vendor interest that evaporates; mitigated by documented commitments in the plan (steps 2–3)
- **Vendor-fatigue risk**: the same vendors fund every event and disengage; mitigated by rotating funding targets across the vendor base (step 1)
System Touchpoints: - Vendor-funded promotional opportunity identification per event (step 1)
- Vendor commitment solicitation — catalog placement, endcaps, features (step 2)
- Promotional plan compilation — committed vendor funding vs. BuildRight spend (step 3)
Time Estimate: 2–3 weeks elapsed per occurrence (1–2 weeks + 1 week); cadence-carried steps as authored (1–2 weeks/cycle) — at ~6–10 promotional plans/year ≈ 6–10 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: For each promotional event: CMO and Category Managers identify vendor-funded promotional opportunities: (a) which vendors will participate in the catalog feature, (b) which vendors will fund endcap displays, (c) which vendors will provide promotional pricing (vendor absorbs markdown cost), (d) which vendors will contribute to digital marketing campaign, (e) target: vendor funding covers 30–50% of total promotional marketing cost

Category Managers contact vendors with promotional proposals: (a) catalog placement offer (with pricing), (b) endcap display opportunity (with expected traffic and sales lift), (c) digital advertising package (with audience reach), (d) vendor responds with commitment and budget

CMO compiles vendor commitments into promotional plan: (a) total vendor funding committed, (b) BuildRight's own marketing spend, (c) combined promotional plan with activity schedule, (d) ROI projection: expected sales lift vs. total promotional cost

fields.Participants: Marketing Team, Category Managers, Vendors, Stores

workflows.name: Co-Op Marketing Activity Execution & Vendor Notification

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "print and digital" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-log of "Vendor notification of activity execution" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-send of "sends display setup instructions to stores" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-359 (ensure controlled execution — Co-Op Marketing & Promotional Fund Management (PA-39.2).)
- operational: Marketing Team review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Non-compliant-execution risk**: stores skip or misinstall displays, voiding reimbursement; mitigated by setup instructions with store compliance confirmation (step 3)
- **Proof-gap risk**: execution happens but proof isn't captured for reimbursement; mitigated by proof-of-execution capture as a required activity step (step 2)
System Touchpoints: - Co-op activity execution — catalogs distributed, displays set per vendor agreement (step 1)
- Proof-of-execution capture — display photos, digital screenshots, circulation proof (step 2)
- Store display compliance workflow with planogram adherence (step 3)
Time Estimate: Per co-op activity ~1–2 days of execution-verification effort (proof-of-execution documentation 1–2 days post-execution + store display compliance within the promotional period) × ~50–100 activities/year ≈ 50–200 days/year.

steps.activity: Execute co-op marketing activity per plan: (a) catalog distributed (print and digital), (b) in-store displays set up per vendor-approved layout, (c) social media posts published with vendor product features, (d) email campaign sent to loyalty members, (e) digital ads launched on Facebook, Google, and marketplace platforms

Vendor notification of activity execution: (a) send vendor proof of execution (photos of displays, screenshots of digital ads, catalog copies), (b) activity dates and scope confirmation, (c) any deviations from agreed plan documented and explained

Store compliance: (a) marketing sends display setup instructions to stores, (b) stores execute display per planogram, (c) store sends photo confirmation to marketing, (d) marketing verifies compliance and addresses non-compliant stores

fields.Volume: 1 proof-of-performance package per activity per vendor

workflows.name: Co-Op Marketing Expense Documentation & Proof of Performance

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-generate of "print costs, ad placement fees, display materials" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-document of "documentation per vendor agreement present" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-submit of "submitted to vendor" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-359 (ensure controlled execution — Co-Op Marketing & Promotional Fund Management (PA-39.2).)
- operational: Marketing Team review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Incomplete-package risk**: reimbursement denied for missing documentation elements; mitigated by the AP completeness checklist per agreement (step 2)
- **Retention-gap risk**: POP lost before disputes or audits; mitigated by on-file retention of all submissions (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Proof-of-performance (POP) package compilation — expense invoices, proof of execution, claim summary (step 1)
- AP completeness review against vendor agreement requirements (step 2)
- POP submission via vendor portal or email, retained on file (step 3)
Time Estimate: 2 days elapsed per occurrence (1 day + 1 day); cadence-carried steps as authored (1–2 days/activity) — at ~50–100 documentation packages/year ≈ 50–100 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: Marketing Team compiles proof-of-performance (POP) documentation: (a) invoice/receipt for marketing expenses (print costs, ad placement fees, display materials), (b) photos of in-store displays (front view, side view, product close-up with pricing), (c) screenshots of digital ads (with date, platform, reach/impressions metrics), (d) catalog copy with vendor product placement highlighted, (e) sales report for promoted items during activity period (vs. baseline), (f) activity summary: dates, stores participating, results

POP package reviewed by AP Manager for completeness: (a) all required documentation per vendor agreement present, (b) expense amounts match invoices, (c) photos meet vendor requirements (clear, dated, correct stores), (d) any missing documentation requested from Marketing before submission
POP package submitted to vendor: (a) via vendor portal (preferred), (b) via email to vendor marketing contact, (c) retained in system for audit trail

workflows.name: Vendor Co-Op Fund Reimbursement Claim & Settlement

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-document of "documentation insufficient, expense not eligible, execution not per agreement" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-record of "records co-op fund income" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-escalate of "escalate to Category Manager for vendor relationship discussion" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-359 (ensure controlled execution — Co-Op Marketing & Promotional Fund Management (PA-39.2).)
- operational: AP Manager review and approval gate; periodic reconciliation against source documents
Pain Points / Risks: - **Partial-denial drift**: short reimbursements accepted silently, eroding fund value; mitigated by dispute resolution with documentation (step 3)
- **Fund-balance-blindness risk**: remaining balances and unapproved claims lose visibility; mitigated by the quarterly per-vendor reconciliation (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Vendor reimbursement approval/denial intake (30–60 day cycle) (step 1)
- Approved reimbursement processing — credit note to AP or cash receipt (step 2)
- Dispute resolution with additional documentation (step 3)
- Quarterly per-vendor fund reconciliation — budget, claimed, approved, received (step 4)
Time Estimate: 4.3–8.6 weeks elapsed per occurrence (30–60 days); cadence-carried steps as authored (Per settlement, As needed, 1 day/quarter) — at ~50–100 claims/year ≈ 50–100 occurrences/year.

steps.activity: Vendor reviews POP and approves/denies reimbursement: (a) typical review period: 30–60 days, (b) approval: vendor issues credit note or payment, (c) partial approval: vendor disputes portion of claim (documentation insufficient, expense not eligible, execution not per agreement), (d) denial: vendor rejects claim with reason

AP Manager processes approved reimbursement: (a) credit note: applied to vendor AP balance (reduces next payment to vendor), (b) cash payment: received in bank account; Treasury confirms and applies, (c) system records co-op fund income: debit cash/AP, credit co-op marketing income (contra-marketing expense)

Dispute resolution: (a) if vendor partially denies: Marketing Team provides additional documentation or accepts denial, (b) if vendor fully denies: escalate to Category Manager for vendor relationship discussion, (c) unresolved disputes > 90 days: written off; co-op fund income reduced accordingly
Quarterly: AP Manager reconciles co-op fund activity per vendor: (a) annual budget, (b) claimed amount, (c) approved and received, (d) pending, (e) denied, (f) remaining fund balance available

fields.Participants: VP Merchandising, Category Managers, Store Managers, Vendors
fields.Volume: ~200 stores × ~10–15 paid display locations = 2,000–3,000 vendor-funded displays active at any time

workflows.name: In-Store Vendor Display & Endcap Program Management

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-schedule of "schedule rotated monthly or per promotional cycle" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-send of "sends photo confirmation to Category Manager" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "reviews display performance" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-359 (ensure controlled execution — Co-Op Marketing & Promotional Fund Management (PA-39.2).)
- operational: VP Merchandising review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Paid-slot-underperformance risk**: premium slots sold to vendors without delivering sales lift, souring renewals; mitigated by performance tracking informing next rotations (step 3)
- **Execution-decay risk**: displays degrade mid-program; mitigated by store execution standards and rotation discipline (step 2)
System Touchpoints: - Paid display program — premium locations (endcaps, feature tables, entrances) per store (step 1)
- Store display execution per planogram with vendor-provided materials (step 2)
- Display performance tracking — sales lift vs. baseline (step 3)
Time Estimate: Monthly display rotation: store setup labor ~1–2 days per store across its 10–15 paid display locations ≈ 8–16 hours/store/month ≈ 1,600–3,200 hours/month chain-wide at 200 stores — standing merchandising labor on 2,000–3,000 active vendor-funded displays; program planning and monthly performance tracking ≈ 2–3 days/month.

steps.activity: VP Merchandising manages paid display program: (a) premium display locations identified per store: endcaps, feature tables, entrance displays, power aisle stacks, (b) pricing per display location per month (e.g., endcap: PHP 10–20K/month; entrance feature: PHP 30–50K/month), (c) vendors pay for premium placement via co-op fund, (d) display schedule rotated monthly or per promotional cycle

Store execution: (a) Store Manager receives display plan from merchandising, (b) sets up display per planogram and vendor-provided materials, (c) sends photo confirmation to Category Manager, (d) non-compliant stores flagged and corrected
Performance tracking: Category Manager reviews display performance (sales lift for displayed items vs. baseline); high-performing displays extended; underperforming displays rotated

fields.Participants: CMO, Digital Marketing Team, Vendor, Agency

workflows.name: Vendor-Funded Digital Marketing & Social Media Campaign

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-post of "posts featuring vendor products" (replaces manual Step 1).
- System auto-track of "commits funding amount" — vendor-approved campaign budget and creative (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-schedule of "ads launched per schedule" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-359 (ensure controlled execution — Co-Op Marketing & Promotional Fund Management (PA-39.2).)
- operational: CMO review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Brand-approval-bypass risk**: ads run without vendor creative approval, voiding funding; mitigated by approval workflow before launch (step 2)
- **Cost-documentation gap**: digital costs (platform, agency, influencer fees) under-documented for claims; mitigated by invoice capture in the claim package (step 4)
System Touchpoints: - Vendor-funded digital campaign proposal — social, search, influencer (step 1)
- Vendor approval of budget and creative per brand guidelines (step 2)
- Campaign execution with real-time performance tracking (impressions, ROAS) (step 3)
- Digital co-op claim with platform/agency/influencer invoices (step 4)
Time Estimate: ~2–4 days per vendor-funded digital campaign (proposal + vendor approval + launch management + co-op claim documentation) × ~10–20 campaigns/year ≈ 20–80 days/year on ~PHP 10–20M vendor funding.

steps.activity: Digital Marketing Team proposes vendor-funded digital campaign: (a) Facebook/Instagram sponsored posts featuring vendor products, (b) Google Shopping ads for vendor category, (c) YouTube how-to videos featuring vendor tools/products, (d) influencer partnerships (local DIY/construction content creators), (e) marketplace (Shopee/Lazada) featured listings, (f) each proposal includes: expected reach, engagement rate, cost, and vendor contribution request

Vendor approves digital campaign budget and creative: (a) vendor provides brand guidelines, (b) approves ad copy and visuals, (c) commits funding amount, (d) BuildRight executes campaign and tracks performance

Campaign execution: (a) ads launched per schedule, (b) real-time performance tracking (impressions, clicks, conversions, ROAS), (c) mid-campaign optimization (adjust targeting, creative, budget allocation), (d) post-campaign report shared with vendor
Co-op claim: digital campaign costs documented (ad platform invoices, agency fees, influencer fees); POP submitted to vendor per W1799

fields.Participants: FP&A, CMO, Category Managers, VP Merchandising
fields.Trigger: Post-campaign analysis; quarterly vendor business review

workflows.name: Co-Op Marketing ROI Analysis & Vendor Reporting

Automation Opportunity: - System auto-log of "catalog, digital, in-store display" (replaces manual Step 2).
- System auto-review of "Vendor business review" (replaces manual Step 3).
Controls: - CTL-359 (ensure controlled execution — Co-Op Marketing & Promotional Fund Management (PA-39.2).)
- operational: FP&A review and approval gate
Pain Points / Risks: - **Vanity-metric risk**: campaigns judged on impressions rather than incremental margin; mitigated by ROI analysis anchored on baseline lift (step 1)
- **Value-undemonstrated risk**: vendors can't see what their funding earned, weakening renewals; mitigated by quarterly vendor business reviews (step 3)
System Touchpoints: - Per-campaign ROI analysis — incremental sales/margin vs. baseline (step 1)
- Quarterly aggregate — co-op funding received vs. marketing spend (step 2)
- Vendor business review presentation of co-op results (step 3)
Time Estimate: Per-campaign ROI analysis 1–2 days × ~50–100 campaign analyses/year ≈ 50–200 days/year; quarterly aggregate co-op review 1 day ≈ 4 days/year; vendor business reviews quarterly with key vendors.

steps.activity: Per-campaign ROI analysis: (a) incremental sales during campaign period (vs. baseline), (b) incremental gross margin (net of promotional markdown and BuildRight's marketing spend), (c) vendor co-op funding received (or expected), (d) net cost to BuildRight = marketing spend − vendor funding, (e) ROI = incremental margin ÷ net cost, (f) campaign effectiveness metrics: reach, conversion rate, ATV lift

Quarterly aggregate: (a) total vendor co-op funding received vs. marketing spend, (b) co-op as % of total marketing budget, (c) ROI by vendor and by campaign type (catalog, digital, in-store display), (d) vendor ranking: highest co-op contributors and best ROI performers

Vendor business review: Category Managers present co-op marketing results to key vendors: (a) campaign performance, (b) sales growth attributable to co-op activities, (c) proposal for next period co-op budget (increase for high-ROI activities), (d) strengthen vendor partnership based on mutual benefit
